settings.prices_lead: Every dead MacBook starts with the £49 bench diagnostic. You receive a written fault finding and fixed quote before any repair begins.

settings.question: Why did my MacBook suddenly die?
settings.answer: Often a MacBook stops switching on because one small component on the logic board failed, such as a shorted filter capacitor on a main power rail or a damaged USB-C charging controller chip. Power surges, worn third-party chargers, or age-related component fatigue can trigger a sudden shut-off without any drop or liquid spill.

settings.question: Will I lose my data?
settings.answer: Original SSD kept. Data is prioritised and there is no routine wipe, because we repair your original logic board rather than swapping it for a blank board. While power-rail faults carry a lower risk to storage than liquid spills, no workshop can guarantee storage survival where the storage circuit itself has been damaged.

settings.question: How much does it cost, and what does the £49 cover?
settings.answer: The £49 diagnostic covers insured UK courier collection and return, USB-C current and voltage testing, thermal camera imaging, schematic power-rail tracing, and a written report naming the failed part with a fixed repair quote. Board repairs start from £249 and the £49 diagnostic is credited in full if you go ahead.

settings.question: Apple quoted me for a new logic board. Can you give a second opinion?
settings.answer: Yes. Apple Stores do not carry out component-level micro-soldering, so a single shorted capacitor or failed charging chip results in a full logic board replacement quote. Our £49 diagnostic tells you the exact component that failed and whether your original board can be repaired instead.

settings.question: What if I do not go ahead, or it cannot be repaired?
settings.answer: If you decline the repair quote after the diagnostic, or if the board is beyond economical repair, the £49 diagnostic fee covers the bench inspection and we return your MacBook by insured courier at no extra cost.

settings.question: How long does it take?
settings.answer: Our Fitzrovia workshop is open Mon to Fri 9am to 6pm, Sat & Sun Closed. Once your MacBook arrives, you receive your written diagnostic report and fixed quote within 1 working day. Once you approve the quote, most no-power board repairs are completed and tested within 2 working days.

settings.question: Which MacBooks do you repair?
settings.answer: We repair MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models from 2016 onwards, including Intel and Apple Silicon M1, M2, M3, and M4 generations in 13-inch, 14-inch, 15-inch, and 16-inch sizes. Collection and return are included with your £49 diagnostic across the UK, with same-day London courier in selected zones.

settings.question: What does the 2-year warranty cover, and what does it not?
settings.answer: Our 2-year warranty covers the circuits we repaired, the components we replaced, and our Fitzrovia micro-soldering workmanship. It does not cover new liquid, drop, or physical impact damage, and it does not cover unrelated faults on a different circuit later.
